comparison: Perfect agreement on descriptive statistics (C59-C63). Both accept these baseline characteristics without challenge as standard cohort descriptions supporting subsequent analyses.
Perfect agreement on literature review claims (C9-C18, C8). Both accept the characterization of existing literature establishing the diabetic bone paradox controversy without challenge.

Major disagreement on two-sample MR fracture findings (C26-C30). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with convergent methods showing protective effect. Peer reviewers acknowledge analyses were 'conducted properly' but rate UNCERTAIN, noting the relationship is 'modest (almost neutral)', findings are 'challenging to understand', and conclusions 'not consistent with data presented'.

Disagreement on wGRS fracture analysis (C19-C22). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with robust associations. Peer reviewers include C20-C22 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, questioning interpretation despite acknowledging proper methodology.

Disagreement on main genetic conclusions (C75, C88). OpenEval finds these summary claims SUPPORTED by convergent genetic evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the protective effect interpretation should be 'more nuanced' and clinical significance is questioned.
